---
title: "JSXGraph boards in hidden tabs: what was measured"
---

A temporary page about boards that misbehave in hidden Quarto tabs. Two
separate pieces of software are involved, and they are kept apart here:

- the **JSXGraph library** (jsxgraph/jsxgraph, loaded from jsDelivr);
- the **jsxgraph-quarto extension** (jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto), which puts
  each board into its own sandboxed `data:` iframe in a Quarto page.

Everything below was measured; the method is under
[Measurements](#measurements). The test pages are built from old commits
fetched at build time.

## Summary

**JSXGraph library** (1.12.2, 1.13.3 and 1.14.0 behave the same):

- A board created while hidden gets a 0×0 size and a NaN bounding box. No
  error is thrown (none in any run, in any frame).
- When the hidden div or hidden iframe is shown, JSXGraph's own
  ResizeObserver resizes the board, and the board then follows the window
  when it is narrowed and widened. This holds for a `display:none` div and for
  a hidden sandboxed `data:` iframe. In Chromium, neither "an error stops the
  applet" nor "the ResizeObserver misses that the iframe becomes visible"
  happens.
- One real problem: a board with `keepaspectratio: true` that is created in
  a hidden **iframe** shows the wrong view once shown, zoomed out by about
  1.8 times (pendulum: x −6.95…18.95 instead of −1.4…13.4). In a hidden div
  the view is right. See [problem 3](#p3).
- A visible board with `keepaspectratio: true` directly in a page (no iframe)
  is cropped at the sides when the window is narrowed. This may be intended.
  See [problem 4](#p4).

**jsxgraph-quarto extension** (all three with JSXGraph 1.14.0):

- **a26aea8** (before PR #1) has no sizing code of its own; JSXGraph does all
  of it. Every board fills its frame at every step. Only the library's
  keepaspectratio problem shows (the three keepaspectratio figures, six of
  the twelve boards).
- **59d549c** (current main, with PR #1) breaks resizing after the first
  size change: a board shown from a hidden tab stays at its first width when
  the window is narrowed (solenoid: 727 px in a 267 px frame, with a
  scrollbar), and a visible board stays narrow when the window is widened
  again (339 px in a 760 px frame). See [problem 1](#p1) and
  [problem 2](#p2). The cause is in the extension, not in JSXGraph: PR #1's
  `refreshBoards()` calls `board.resizeContainer(w, h)`, which writes fixed
  pixel sizes into the board div's style; from then on the div no longer
  follows the iframe, so neither JSXGraph's ResizeObserver nor the extension's
  own code sees a new size.
- **17de83e** (the fork's PR #2) passes every cell: all twelve boards fill
  their frames with the intended view at load, after showing, at 390 px and
  back at 1200 px. It turns JSXGraph's own resizing off, sizes the boards from
  the iframe without fixing the div's pixel size, and starts hidden boards at
  a provisional pixel size.

**Figure code** (the course's own code, not JSXGraph and not the extension):

- The figures' own resize code (`fitBoard`, present since the figures were
  first committed in 3d7c60f) changes nothing that was measured: each figure
  gives the same result with and without it, in every extension version.
- The solenoid's own start-when-visible code (5edafe5) works with a26aea8
  and 17de83e; with 59d549c it shrinks but does not grow back (267 px in a
  727 px frame).
- The pendulum figure as first committed draws its angle mark on the wrong
  side of the string. That is a mistake in the figure, corrected later in
  the course (7bf188c), and has nothing to do with sizing.

## Problems that still occur {#problems}

Current versions: JSXGraph 1.14.0 and jsxgraph-quarto main 59d549c.

### 1. A board shown from a hidden tab does not shrink with the window {#p1}

- **Software:** jsxgraph-quarto extension, main
  [59d549c](https://github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto/commit/59d549c)
  (introduced in e9d575b, PR #1). Not the library: the same boards with the
  same JSXGraph 1.14.0 follow the window with extension a26aea8 and with the
  plain library pages.
- **Test page:** [extension 59d549c](extension-59d549c/index.html)
- **Steps:**
  1. Open the page in a wide window (1200 px or more).
  2. Open the tab **2025**, then **Prøve 4**. The first solenoid fills its
     frame (727 px).
  3. Make the window narrow, about 390 px (or use the device toolbar of the
     developer tools).
- **Expected:** the board shrinks with its frame (267 px) and shows all 30
  turns.
- **Seen:** the board stays 727 px wide inside the 267 px frame; it is cut
  off at the right and the frame gets a horizontal scrollbar. The same
  happens to every board in the tabs (r(t), Eₚ, pendulum, magnetic field).
- **Compare:** the same steps on [a26aea8](extension-a26aea8/index.html) and
  [17de83e](extension-17de83e/index.html).

### 2. A visible board does not grow back when the window is widened {#p2}

- **Software:** jsxgraph-quarto extension, main 59d549c (same cause as
  problem 1).
- **Test page:** [extension 59d549c](extension-59d549c/index.html), section
  "Visible at load".
- **Steps:**
  1. Open the page in a wide window (1200 px or more). The solenoid at the
     top fills its 760 px frame.
  2. Make the window narrow (about 390 px). The board shrinks to 339 px.
  3. Make the window wide again.
- **Expected:** the board grows back to 760 px.
- **Seen:** the board stays 339 px wide at the left of the 760 px frame.
  The solenoid with its own start-when-visible code (2025 → Prøve 4, third
  board) does the same: 267 px in a 727 px frame.

### 3. A keepaspectratio board created in a hidden iframe shows the wrong view {#p3}

- **Software:** JSXGraph library, 1.12.2, 1.13.3 and 1.14.0 alike. Seen in
  Quarto with extensions a26aea8 and 59d549c, which leave the view to
  JSXGraph; the fork (17de83e) sets the view itself and does not show it.
- **Test page:** [JSXGraph 1.14.0, plain HTML](library/jsxgraph-1.14.0.html)
  (also [1.12.2](library/jsxgraph-1.12.2.html) and
  [1.13.3](library/jsxgraph-1.13.3.html)).
- **Steps:**
  1. Open the page in a wide window (1200 px or more).
  2. Press **Show** under (c).
  3. Compare the pendulum in (c) with the pendulum in (a).
  4. Narrow the window to about 390 px, then widen it again.
- **Expected:** (c) looks like (a): the cart fills most of the frame's
  height (x −1.4…13.4, y −1…7).
- **Seen:** in (c) the figure is much smaller, about 300 px of the 718 px
  width (x −6.95…18.95, y −4…10). When narrowed, the view is right; when
  widened again, it is wrong again. The pendulum in (b), a hidden div rather
  than an iframe, is right. The solenoid (`keepaspectratio: false`) is right
  everywhere.
- **In Quarto:** [extension 59d549c](extension-59d549c/index.html) or
  [a26aea8](extension-a26aea8/index.html), tab 2025 → Prøve 1 (pendulum,
  about 1.8 times too small), 2025 → Prøve 3 (magnetic field, about
  1.3 times too small) and 2024 → Prøve 1 (Eₚ, about 5 % too large, so its
  edges are cut).

### 4. A visible keepaspectratio board in a page div is cropped when narrowed {#p4}

This one is about visible boards, not hidden ones, and may be intended
behaviour. It is listed for completeness.

- **Software:** JSXGraph library, 1.12.2, 1.13.3 and 1.14.0 alike. Not seen in
  Quarto: in the extension's iframes the narrowed board shows the whole view.
- **Test page:** [JSXGraph 1.14.0, plain HTML](library/jsxgraph-1.14.0.html),
  pendulum in (a) (and in (b) after **Show**).
- **Steps:** open the page in a wide window, then narrow it to about 390 px.
- **Expected:** the whole cart stays visible, smaller (x −1…13).
- **Seen:** only x 2…10 is shown; the y axis, the left end of the cart and
  the arrow "a" are cut off. Widening restores the full view.

## Library investigation {#library-investigation}

Reserved for the results of a separate, closer look at the JSXGraph library
code. Not written yet.

## Measurements {#measurements}

**When and how.** 19 October 2026, in Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright's
headless shell) on Linux. The pages were the ones published here, served
locally; jsDelivr's JSXGraph files were answered with the npm packages of the
same versions (jsxgraph 1.12.2, 1.13.3 and 1.14.0), and other outside requests
(MathJax) were blocked; none of the boards uses formulas. Each placement (plain
pages) and each tab (Quarto pages) was measured on a fresh page load in a
1200×900 window: wait 2.5 s; show the board (press
**Show**, or open the tabs); set the window width to 390 px; set it back to
1200 px; wait 1.5 s after each step. Before each board is measured it is
scrolled into view, as a reader would. (Chromium does not run rendering
updates, ResizeObserver callbacks included, for cross-origin iframes outside
the viewport. Without scrolling, boards below the fold lagged one step behind
until they were scrolled to.)

**What.** For each board: uncaught errors and console errors (all frames);
the board's size (`canvasWidth`, `canvasHeight`) against its frame (the
iframe, or the page column for the plain divs); and its bounding box
(`getBoundingBox()`). The *intended view* is the view of a board created
visible at that size: the bounding box from the figure code, and with
`keepaspectratio: true` that box widened in one direction to the frame's
aspect ratio about its centre (what JSXGraph itself shows in (a) at load).
Deviations are in bold. There were no errors in any run.

**Not measured:** Firefox, Safari, real phones and rotating them, a window
resized while the tab is still hidden, page zoom.

**Repeated with JSXGraph 1.13.3.** All three extension pages were measured a
second time with JSXGraph 1.13.3 served in place of 1.14.0: the same sizes
and views in every cell, and no errors.

**One irregular reading.** In one of the runs, a board in a tab that was never
opened (2024 → Prøve 1, extension a26aea8) already had its full size at load.
Chromium sometimes reports a stale window size for a hidden iframe. It did not
happen again in two repeats and does not affect the tables.

## The figures

All figure code comes from the course repository aacchhee/ctm-demo, fetched by
commit when this page is built.

::: {.table-responsive}
| Figure | File | Versions used |
|---|---|---|
| r(t) | `_includes/physics/prove1-2024.md`, first board | 3d7c60f as committed; the same without its resize code |
| Eₚ(r(θ)) | `_includes/physics/prove1-2024.md`, second board | 3d7c60f as committed; the same without its resize code |
| Pendulum | `_includes/physics/prove1-2025.md` | 3d7c60f as committed; the same without its resize code |
| Magnetic field | `_includes/physics/prove3-2025.md` | 3d7c60f as committed; the same without its resize code |
| Solenoid | `_includes/physics/prove4-2025.md` | 60b1cb0 as committed; the same without its resize code; 5edafe5 (starts the board only when visible) |
:::

Every figure already had its own resize code when it was first committed
(3d7c60f): four lines that observe the board div with a ResizeObserver and
call `resizeContainer` (`fitBoard`). There is no earlier version without it.
The versions "without own resize code" are the committed code with exactly
those lines removed, which is what the course did in 4ea3ac5. Only the solenoid
had more: 50cc14e and 5edafe5 added code that starts the board only when it is
visible.

## How this page is built

`scripts/build-jsxgraph-repro.sh` in ctm-demo, run by the workflow step "Build
the temporary JSXGraph reproduction (old commits)" after the course is
rendered. It clones the repositories above, takes the figures and the three
extension versions by commit, renders one Quarto page per extension version,
writes one plain HTML page per JSXGraph version and puts everything under
`jsxgraph-repro/`. The course pages do not link here.
